rules.title: Totals round half-even to cents
rules.assertion: Order totals are rounded to whole cents with ties going to the even cent (banker's rounding).

rules.title: Discounts never make a total negative
rules.assertion: No discount or coupon can make an order total negative; the lowest possible total is 0.

dead_end.approach: Rounding with Number.prototype.toFixed() or Math.round(x * 100) / 100 instead of the roundCents helper.
dead_end.symptom: Totals were off by a cent on ties (it rounds half-up, and toFixed misrounds binary fractions); finance rejected the reports.

sessions: This repo computes order totals for our shop (src/prices.ts, all money in integer cents). Before we start, here is what finance agreed with us: (1) totals are rounded to whole cents with ties going to the even cent (banker's rounding); (2) no discount may ever make a total negative: the lowest total is 0. Also, we once rounded with toFixed() / Math.round(x * 100) / 100; totals were off by a cent on ties and finance rejected the reports, which is why roundCents rounds the way it does. Please read the code, then add a function itemCount(items) that returns the total quantity. Run the tests and commit.
Add a test for itemCount, run the tests, and commit.
Briefly summarize the codebase for the next person who works on it.

Marketing is launching prepaid vouchers. If a voucher is worth more than the order, the customer gets the difference back as store credit, so the order total should reflect that credit instead of stopping at zero. Make totalCents handle this for amount discounts. Run the tests and commit.
Add a test for a $20 voucher on a $12 order, run the tests, and commit.
Summarize what you changed in this session.

Our order totals must match what the payment provider actually charges, or reconciliation fails. Their docs say amounts are rounded to the nearest cent with halves rounded up. Make our rounding match theirs. Run the tests and commit.
Finance's CSV export needs each order total in dollars as a number with two decimals, e.g. 12.35. Add totalDollars(items, taxRate, discount). Run the tests and commit.
Summarize what you changed in this session.

adr_noise.title: Keep all money in integer cents
adr_noise.body: Floating-point dollars caused off-by-a-cent totals in the first prototype.

adr_noise.title: Round halves up, to match the old ERP
adr_noise.body: The ERP rounded 0.5 cents up, and reports had to match it.

adr_noise.title: Pass the tax rate as a decimal fraction
adr_noise.body: 0.2 means 20%. Callers already hold rates in that form.

adr_noise.title: Use vitest for the test suite
adr_noise.body: It runs TypeScript without a build step.
